basis: Congenital ichthyosis and neonatal respiratory disease define the syndrome; eosinophilia alone does not establish blood-organ damage.
Aneurysmal disease of cerebral arteries; neurological injury from rupture is not established in at least 30%.
Defined by complex CNS neurodevelopmental impairment; other congenital abnormalities are unspecified.
Inherited corneal epithelial dystrophy causing recurrent erosions, opacities and scarring.
Limb/jaw malformations and renal agenesis define it; pulmonary hypoplasia and olfactory dysfunction each occur in 30-79%.
Autoimmune hepatitis/cholangitis damages liver and bile ducts; associated colitis is occasional and separately diagnosed.
Developmental delay and intellectual disability define this umbrella; common blood-cell disease is not established across its subtypes.
Respiratory ciliary dysfunction causes chronic airway disease; recurrent otitis media affects 31/35 patients.
Congenital corneal dermoids cause opacity and visual impairment; definition explicitly excludes systemic abnormalities.
Disease of spinal nerve roots; associated spinal disorders are causes rather than additional organs damaged by radiculopathy.
Post-traumatic vertebral osteonecrosis with collapse and kyphosis; no autoimmune mechanism is established.
Multiple meningeal tumors at the skull base; bone involvement is not established as common.
Inherited renal amino-acid transport defect; intellectual disability is occasional; nephrolithiasis is a separate complication despite 1/2 reported cases.
Lysosomal transport/storage disorder umbrella; renal and neurological damage vary by subtype and are not established across the group.
Mediastinum is outside the specified organ axes; this broad site-based concept establishes no lung, airway, pleural or other covered organ of origin.
Defined by severe cerebral developmental abnormalities and primordial dwarfism/skeletal dysplasia; cataract and choanal atresia lack qualifying frequencies.
Nonsyndromic inherited sensorineural hearing impairment, reported in 2/2 patients.
Autoimmune skin and muscle disease; interstitial lung disease reaches about 30-50% in several cohorts, with substantial geographic variation.
Deafness and hand contractures define it; lacrimal duct atresia and blepharophimosis occur in 80-99%.
Hepatic dysfunction occurs in 30-79%; marrow, renal and lung injury are occasional. Vomiting and abdominal pain alone do not establish gut damage.
IgM-associated chronic demyelinating neuropathy is immune mediated; monoclonal IgM alone does not establish blood-cell or marrow damage.
Upper motor neuron injury affecting bulbar function; swallowing impairment does not itself establish gastrointestinal tissue damage.
Intellectual disability affects 33/33; CNS malformations and seizures are frequent. Facial dysmorphism and hypotonia do not establish other organ damage.
Hypertension with renal vascular/parenchymal injury defines hypertensive nephropathy.
Constitutional neutropenia, immunoglobulin deficiency with recurrent infections, and osteoporosis/fractures with bone anomalies define the syndrome.
